as_told.title: DOE NEST teams as Weygandt's recovery team

plain: The "DOE" people said to have cleaned up a crashed craft in Peru in 1997, in the account of a man named Jonathan Weygandt, were most likely the Department of Energy's Nuclear Emergency Support Team, a hazardous-materials squad known as NEST. That is the reading of a researcher who goes by UAPGerb, who tells Michels this on two occasions, once pointing to the Atomic Energy Act passed by Congress on August 30, 1954, and once to the Wilson-Davis memo, said to be the physicist Eric Davis's notes of a meeting with Admiral Thomas Wilson, while also linking the contractor EG&G. If true, a known nuclear emergency team would double as a crash retrieval unit.
